narrative: At 21:30 on 14 August 1952, two USAF radar operators and a control-tower officer at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base observed a silent disc-shaped object with a steady white glow hovering at high altitude for roughly 8 minutes before departing at high speed to the northwest. The object was briefly tracked on radar. Air Technical Intelligence Center (ATIC) investigators interviewed the witnesses. Project Blue Book adjudicated the case as ASTRONOMICAL — the planet Venus, prominent in the western sky that evening.

A maintenance crew at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base reported three steady amber lights moving in formation across the night sky on 21 September 1952. The lights made a low hum. ATIC reviewed flight logs and concluded the objects were a flight of conventional military aircraft on a night training sortie. Disposition: AIRCRAFT.

On 3 February 1953 a civilian observer near Wright-Patterson Air Force Base reported a slow-moving silver sphere drifting east at high altitude in daylight. Office of Special Investigations (OSI) personnel correlated the sighting with a scheduled research balloon launch. Disposition: BALLOON (research).

At 02:10 on 17 June 1953, a radar operator and two pilots at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base tracked a silent disc executing erratic high-speed maneuvers, including an abrupt right-angle turn, for 12 minutes. Weather was clear with no temperature inversion. ATIC investigators could not reconcile the radar return with any known aircraft, balloon, or astronomical body. Project Blue Book listed the case as UNIDENTIFIED.

Several base personnel at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base reported a brilliant green light descending rapidly on 2 November 1954. ATIC matched the report to a documented fireball (meteor) over the Ohio Valley the same night. Disposition: ASTRONOMICAL (meteor).

On 8 July 1951 a test pilot near Edwards Air Force Base observed a silver cigar-shaped object on a steady high-speed course. Project staff identified it as a high-altitude experimental aircraft under test at the range. Disposition: AIRCRAFT.

A radar site at Edwards Air Force Base recorded an intermittent fast-moving return on 12 May 1952 with no corresponding visual contact. ATIC attributed the track to a radar anomaly (anomalous propagation). Disposition: SENSOR_ARTIFACT.

On 30 March 1955 ground crew near Edwards Air Force Base reported a shifting V-formation of pale objects at low altitude in daylight. OSI investigators concluded the objects were a flock of migratory birds catching the sun. Disposition: BIRD.

Before dawn on 25 July 1948 two airline pilots near Maxwell Air Force Base reported a wingless cigar-shaped craft with a double row of glowing windows that passed close to their aircraft and climbed steeply. Project Sign investigators interviewed the crew. No conventional explanation was established; the case was carried as UNIDENTIFIED.

On 6 November 1957 a sentry near Kirtland Air Force Base reported a glowing orange sphere hovering low over the desert. Investigators noted a strong temperature inversion that night and attributed the sighting to a refraction/mirage effect. Disposition: ATMOSPHERIC.

On 20 March 1966 dozens of civilians and police near Selfridge Air Force Base reported low hovering lights over a marsh. The Air Force consultant attributed the lights to ignited marsh gas and to the planet Venus near the horizon. Disposition: ASTRONOMICAL.

A brief nighttime report on 27 February 1950 near McChord Air Force Base described three dim lights in a triangular arrangement. The single witness could not estimate altitude, size, or duration, and no instrument data existed. Project Grudge marked the case INSUFFICIENT_DATA.

On 19 August 1953 a teenager near Davis-Monthan Air Force Base submitted a photograph of a daytime disc. ATIC analysts determined the image was a thrown hubcap and the report a deliberate hoax. Disposition: HOAX.

On 4 July 1956 observers near Hanscom Field reported colored objects drifting and bursting over the horizon. Investigators identified the source as an Independence Day fireworks display. Disposition: OTHER_IDENTIFIED.

On 12 June 1958 a tower operator at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base reported a fast steady white light crossing the field at night. ATIC matched it to a scheduled jet interceptor on approach. Disposition: AIRCRAFT.

On 4 September 1961 personnel near Wright-Patterson reported a shimmering orange sphere low on the horizon at dusk. A pronounced temperature inversion was logged; investigators attributed the sighting to a mirage of ground lights. Disposition: ATMOSPHERIC.

At 22:05 on 28 July 1952 a radar operator at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base tracked a silent disc holding station northwest of the field for six minutes. Later, at 23:50 the same night, a second disc-shaped object appeared on radar and visually, executing a sharp climb before fading. ATIC could not reconcile either return with known traffic. Project Blue Book carried the case as UNIDENTIFIED.

On 30 January 2024 a perimeter sensor at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base logged a bright fast-moving point with no radar correlate. AARO analysts determined the artifact was a lens flare from a passing vehicle's headlight on the camera housing. Disposition: SENSOR_ARTIFACT.

location: near Edwards Air Force Base, California
narrative: On 17 August 1954 a guard near Edwards Air Force Base reported a brilliant green streak descending at high speed. ATIC matched the report to a Perseid fireball. Disposition: ASTRONOMICAL (meteor).

On 22 March 1958 a flight-line crew at Edwards reported a silver cigar at high altitude leaving a thin trail. Project staff identified an experimental high-altitude aircraft under test. Disposition: AIRCRAFT.

location: near Edwards Air Force Base, California
narrative: On 10 June 1955 observers near Edwards Air Force Base reported a disc making a high pass at 09:15, then a second pass by what appeared to be the same object at 09:40. Range control correlated both passes with a classified test flight. Disposition: AIRCRAFT.

location: near Edwards Air Force Base, California
narrative: On 3 August 1965 several witnesses near Edwards Air Force Base reported a steady bright object low in the west after sunset. Investigators identified the planet Venus at peak brightness. Disposition: ASTRONOMICAL.

On 10 April 1949 observers near Holloman Air Force Base reported a high silver sphere drifting slowly in daylight. Project Sign correlated it with a Skyhook research balloon launch. Disposition: BALLOON (research).

On 13 May 1960 a sentry near Vandenberg Air Force Base reported a steady point of light tracking smoothly across the night sky. Investigators correlated the track with the predicted pass of an early reconnaissance satellite. Disposition: SATELLITE.

On 18 October 1973 security personnel near Minot Air Force Base reported a silent disc with a pulsing red glow hovering over a weapons-storage area, briefly correlated on base radar. Office of Special Investigations could not identify the object. The record was carried as UNIDENTIFIED.

On 27 October 1975 multiple security policemen near Loring Air Force Base reported a low slow-moving object with red and white lights penetrating the base perimeter on consecutive nights. No aircraft was identified on local radar. The northern-tier overflight record was carried as UNIDENTIFIED.

On 11 June 1978 a patrol near Kirtland Air Force Base reported a brilliant slow-falling light. The duty officer correlated it with a documented bolide reported across the Southwest. Disposition: ASTRONOMICAL (fireball).

On 15 January 1980 a gate guard near Beale Air Force Base reported a shifting line of pale objects at low altitude at dawn. Investigators concluded the objects were a flight of waterfowl catching the early light. Disposition: BIRD.

location: off San Diego, near Naval Air Station North Island, California
narrative: On 14 November 2004 F/A-18 aircrew operating from a carrier near Naval Air Station North Island engaged a smooth wingless 'Tic Tac' object that hovered then accelerated beyond visual range. The object was held on AN/SPY-1 radar and forward-looking infrared. AARO carried the Nimitz encounter as UNIDENTIFIED. Detection: VISUAL_RADAR.

location: near Naval Air Station Oceana, Virginia
narrative: During training near Naval Air Station Oceana in November 2014, aircrew recorded an object moving against a strong wind at high speed; a first encounter was logged mid-morning and a second, separate object was recorded the following afternoon. Both were held on sensor pods. AARO carried the East Coast records as UNIDENTIFIED.

On 2 September 2017 base security near Creech Air Force Base observed a small four-rotor object loitering over the perimeter. The object was recovered and identified as a commercial quadcopter operated without authorization. Disposition: UAS_DRONE.

On 24 May 2019 numerous observers near Vandenberg Air Force Base reported an evenly spaced 'train' of moving lights crossing the sky. The objects were identified as a newly launched Starlink satellite batch in low orbit. Disposition: SATELLITE (Starlink).

On 8 September 2020 a sentry near Travis Air Force Base reported steady lights on a level course at night. ADS-B records matched a commercial airliner on a published arrival route. Disposition: AIRCRAFT.

The June 2021 ODNI preliminary assessment reviewed numerous service reports of unidentified aerial phenomena near U.S. training ranges. Most lacked sufficient sensor data to characterize. AARO carried the bulk of the tranche as INSUFFICIENT_DATA.

On 17 March 2022 a sensor near Eglin Air Force Base tracked a slow high-altitude sphere drifting with the prevailing wind. Analysts correlated it with a scientific research balloon release. Disposition: BALLOON (research).

On 19 July 2018 a viral video purported to show a metallic disc near Nellis Air Force Base. AARO and independent analysts determined the clip was a digitally composited fabrication. Disposition: HOAX.

On 11 October 2016 observers near Cannon Air Force Base reported a band of shifting colored light low on the horizon at night. Investigators attributed it to a temperature-inversion mirage of distant city lights. Disposition: ATMOSPHERIC.

location: near Edwards Air Force Base, California
narrative: On 15 August 2023 range security near Edwards Air Force Base detected a small uncrewed aircraft transiting restricted airspace. The object was tracked and identified as a hobbyist drone. Disposition: UAS_DRONE.
